skill.name: azure-cost
skill.description: Queries Azure costs, forecasts future spending, investigates cost anomalies, and produces evidence-based optimization recommendations using Azure APIs, CLI tools, and official pricing.
skill.summary: Analyze Azure spending with cost queries, forecasts, anomaly investigation, and prioritized optimization recommendations.
skill.author: microsoft

security_audit.summary: Review confirmed one high-risk cleanup command that recursively removes a relative temp directory without proving the skill owns it. Two semantic issues remain: unqualified resource deletion advice and budget creation without an explicit approval checkpoint. The other 79 static findings are documentation false positives involving Markdown links, code fences, official URLs, and non-secret environment selectors.

remediation.issue: Cleanup recursively removes the shared relative temp directory.
remediation.suggestion: Use a unique skill-owned directory and delete only files created during the current run after verifying the resolved path.

remediation.issue: The report template describes discovered resources as immediately deletable.
remediation.suggestion: Require dependency checks, utilization validation, a dry run, rollback guidance, and explicit approval before presenting or executing deletion commands.

remediation.issue: The anomaly workflow can create an Azure budget without an approval checkpoint.
remediation.suggestion: Present the proposed amount, scope, dates, thresholds, and recipients, then require explicit confirmation before executing the command.

content.value_statement: Azure spending can be difficult to explain and control. This skill queries costs, forecasts spending, and produces evidence-based optimization recommendations.
actual_capabilities: Queries actual or amortized Azure costs for supported subscription, resource group, management group, and billing scopes.
Groups historical costs by supported dimensions such as service, resource group, tags, or resource identifier.
Forecasts future Azure spending from eligible historical data and distinguishes actual values from forecast values.
Investigates optimization opportunities using Azure Quick Review, Resource Graph, Monitor metrics, and official pricing pages.
Produces prioritized reports with cost baselines, estimated savings, evidence labels, portal links, and implementation guidance.
limitations: Requires authenticated Azure access and reader permissions for cost, resource, and monitoring data.
Forecasts require sufficient history and do not support grouping by service or resource.
Dimension availability, date ranges, row limits, and rate limits vary by Azure scope and agreement.
Generated savings estimates require human validation before resource changes, purchases, deletions, or tier adjustments.

use_cases.title: Explain Monthly Azure Spend
use_cases.description: Break down actual charges by service, resource group, or tag and identify the largest cost drivers.

use_cases.title: Prioritize Cloud Savings
use_cases.description: Combine cost data, utilization metrics, orphaned-resource checks, and validated pricing into a ranked optimization report.

use_cases.title: Investigate AKS Cost Spikes
use_cases.description: Correlate cluster costs with node counts, scaling events, and resource consumption during a reported anomaly window.

prompt_templates.title: Review Current Spend
prompt_templates.prompt: Show month-to-date Azure cost for subscription <subscription-id>, grouped by service. Use actual cost data and state the currency.

prompt_templates.title: Forecast Subscription Cost
prompt_templates.prompt: Forecast Azure spending for subscription <subscription-id> through <date>. Include actual costs, forecast totals, assumptions, and any unavailable-data warning.

prompt_templates.title: Find Optimization Opportunities
prompt_templates.prompt: Analyze the last 30 days for subscription <subscription-id>. Identify orphaned resources and rightsizing opportunities, validate pricing, and estimate monthly savings.

prompt_templates.title: Investigate an AKS Anomaly
prompt_templates.prompt: Investigate the AKS cost spike for cluster <cluster-name> from <start> to <end>. Correlate costs, node metrics, scaling events, and top consumers. Do not modify resources. Propose budget alert settings separately and wait for approval.

output_examples.input: Show this month by service for subscription Production.
Forecast spending through the end of next month.
output_examples.output: Projected total: 24,700 USD. Actual charges cover completed dates, while forecast values cover future dates. The estimate uses available Azure history.

output_examples.input: Find the largest safe savings opportunities.
output: Priority 1: Validate three unattached disks costing about 240 USD monthly before deletion.
Priority 2: Review two low-utilization virtual machines with an estimated 310 USD monthly rightsizing opportunity.
Priority 3: Confirm storage lifecycle requirements before applying a proposed 90-day policy.

best_practices: Query actual costs before estimating savings, and label actual data, metrics, validated pricing, and estimates clearly.
Use the narrowest Azure scope and least-privilege reader roles needed for the analysis.
Require explicit approval, dry-run validation, and rollback guidance before any resource or budget change.
anti_patterns: Do not estimate costs from list prices when actual billing data is available.
Do not treat orphaned-resource scans as proof that deletion is safe.
Do not execute cleanup or Azure mutation commands without validating paths, scope, impact, and user approval.

faq.question: Which Azure scopes are supported?
faq.answer: The skill documents subscription, resource group, management group, and billing account scopes. API capabilities and dimensions vary by scope.

faq.question: Which permissions are required?
faq.answer: Typical analysis needs Cost Management Reader, Monitoring Reader, and Reader roles on the target scope. Some operations may require additional permissions.

faq.question: Can it forecast costs by service?
faq.answer: No. Azure forecast grouping is not supported. Use grouped historical queries beside the overall forecast.

faq.question: Does it change or delete Azure resources?
faq.answer: Most workflows are read-only, but some references include budget, AKS, and implementation commands. Review every change and require explicit approval.

faq.question: How are savings estimates calculated?
faq.answer: The workflow combines actual costs, utilization metrics, Azure recommendations, and official pricing. Estimates still require human validation.

faq.question: Where are reports and query results stored?
faq.answer: The workflow uses local output and temp directories with timestamped reports. Protect billing data and verify cleanup paths before removal.
